Inglewood, California
  January 8, 2019

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  January 8, 2019, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.
  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the
  City Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the
  hour of 2:03p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary/Finance
  Authority Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman/Finance Authority Chairman Butts/Council
  Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales and Franklin; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as
  follows:
  Yvonne Horton  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Wanda Brown  City Treasurer/Treasurer*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  David Esparza  Asst. City Manager/CFO
  Aisha Thompson  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS.  Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any
  item on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member /
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Padilla that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated,
  December 13, 2018, in the amount of $2,198,789.47, dated December 13, 2018, in the
  amount of $106,227.76, and dated January 4, 2019, in the amount of $4,314,768.63 are
  hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority
  Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are so
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132  CLAIMS DENIED.  Letter from the Office of the City Attorney was presented
  recommending denial of the claim filed by Sergio Castellanos for alleged property
  damage on October 31, 2018.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  and carried that the above listed claim be denied.

  1
 January 8, 2019

 101  AGREEMENT NO. 19-077 APPROVED – SOUTH BAY WORKFORCE
  INVESTMENT BOARD (SBWIB). Staff report dated January 8, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval of an Agreement (Contract) by and between the County of Los
  Angeles and the City of Inglewood, serving as the administrative entity for the South Bay
  Workforce Investment Board (SBWIB), for Welfare-to-Work Vocational and Direct
  Services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-077. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  AMENDMENT NO. 3 TO AGREEMENT NO. 10-66 APPROVED – SKY
  POSTERS, INC. Staff report dated January 8, 2019, was presented recommending
  approval of a third amendment to Agreement No. 10-66 with Sky Posters, Inc., to extend
  the display of super graphic wall sign outdoor advertising.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson,
  that the City Council does hereby approve Amendment No. 3 to Agreement No. 10-66.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 178  AGREEMENT NO. 19-078 APPROVED – DR. SUSAN SAXE-CLIFFORD FOR
  PSYCHOLOGICAL EVALUATION SERVICES. Staff report dated January 8, 2019,
  was presented recommending approval of a three-year agreement (with the option to
  extend two (2) additional one (1) year terms) with Dr. Susan Saxe-Clifford for
  psychological evaluation services for the Police Department.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve Agreement No. 19-078 in the annual amount
  of $30,000. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO AGREEMENT NO. 10-065 APPROVED – LOS
  ANGELES COUNTY METROPOLITAN TRANSPORTATION AUTHORITY;
  CITY MANAGER TO EXECUTE AMENDMENT NO. 1 TO FUNDING
  AGREEMENT NO. CFP #F5300 AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated January 8, 2019,
  was presented recommending approval of Amendment No. 1 to Funding Agreement No.
  CFP #F5300 with Los Angeles County Metropolitan Transportation Authority
  (LACMTA) to extend the City of Inglewood ITS-Phase IV Improvements lapse date to
  June 30, 2019.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amendment No. 1 to Funding Agreement
  No. CFP #F5300; and 2) Authorize the City Manager to execute Amendment No. 1 to
  Funding Agreement No. CFP #F5300 on behalf of the City of Inglewood. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 183  PAYMENT APPROVED - THE ADJUL CORPORATION (DBA LEE
  CONSTRUCTION COMPANY). Staff report dated January 8, 2019, was presented
  recommending approval to pay The Adjul Corporation (DBA Lee Construction
  Company) for additional work performed on the replacement of the storm drain at the
  Inglewood Well No. 4 Project.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby approve payment in the amount of $13,339.25. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:

  2
 January 8, 2019

  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  AGREEMENT NO. 19-079(A) APPROVED – MEDINA MASONRY. Staff report
  dated January 8, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an Agreement with
  Medina Masonry to provide walkway rehabilitation and paver masonry services to
  remove roots, level and replace pavers correcting major public safety concerns on the
  walkway between Parking Structure No. 2 and Market Street.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Franklin that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Approve Agreement No. 19-079(A) in the amount of $38,655
  (includes a 15% contingency of $5,042); and 2) Authorize the Mayor to execute the
  Agreement. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Successor Agency Chairman Butts, and seconded by Successor Agency
  Member Franklin that the Successor Agency does hereby 1) Approve Agreement No. 19-
  079(A) in the amount of $38,655 (includes a 15% contingency of $5,042); 2) Authorize
  the Chairman to execute the Agreement; and 3) Approve the use of tax-exempt bond
  funds to fund the work to be performed. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales. Franklin, and Successor
  Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 301  AGREEMENT NO. 18-040(A) APPROVED – TL VETERANS CONSTRUCTION,
  INC. Staff report dated January 8, 2019, was presented recommending approval of an
  Amended and Restated Agreement with TL Veterans Construction, Inc., extending
  Agreement No. 18-040(A) for a period of one year to complete additional painting work
  needed at Parking Structure No. 2.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Franklin that the City
  Council does hereby: 1) Approve Amended and Restated Agreement No. 18-040(A) in
  the amount of $20,933.23 (to be added to the remaining contract allocation of $9,366.80
  for a total amount of $30,300.03); 2) Allow for payments of aforesaid contract allocation
  following approval of invoicing by the City Manager or his designee; and 3) Authorize
  the Mayor to execute the Amended and Restated Agreement. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Successor Agency Chairman Butts, and seconded by Successor Agency
  Member Franklin that the Successor Agency does hereby 1) Approve Amended and
  Restated Agreement No. 18-040(A) in the amount of $20,933.23 (to be added to the
  remaining contract allocation of $9,366.80 for a total amount of $30,300.03); 2) Allow
  for payments of aforesaid contract allocation following approval of invoicing by the
  Executive Director or his designee; 3) Re-approve the use of tax-exempt bonds funds to
  fund the remaining work and payments totaling $30,300.03 to be performed by TL
  Veterans Construction, Inc., as contemplated in the Amended and Restated Agreement;
  and 4) Authorize the Chairman to execute the Amended and Restated Agreement. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Successor Agency Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales. Franklin, and Successor
  Agency Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 101  CITY MANAGER APPROVAL OF “ONE-TIME” MERIT LUMP SUM
  PAYOUTS FOR SEVERAL MEMBERS OF THE INGLEWOOD EXECUTIVE
  ORGANIZATION (IEO) AUTHORIZED. Staff report dated January 8, 2019, was
  presented recommending authorization be given to the City Manager to approve “one-
  time” merit lump sum payouts for several members of the Inglewood Executive
  3
 January 8, 2019

  Organization (IEO), as authorized by the Memorandum of Understanding (MOU)
  between the City and IEO.
  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Dotson
  that the City Council does hereby authorize the City Manager to approve “one-time”
  merit lump sum payouts. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Morales that the City
  Council include the City Manager, Police Chief, and City Attorney to receive a one-time
  merit lump sum payout. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin, and Mayor Butts;
  Noes: None.

 301  ORDINANCE NO. 19-04 ADOPTED - AMENDING INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL
  CODE CHAPTER 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING), ARTICLE 8 (“C-3” HEAVY
  COMMERCIAL ZONE REGULATIONS) TO INCLUDE ZONING CODE
  AMENDMENT NO. 2018-002 (ZCA-2018-002) TO ALLOW C-2A (AIRPORT
  COMMERICIAL) ZONE PERMITTED USES IN THE C-3 (HEAVY
  COMMERCIAL) ZONE CITYWIDE. Staff report dated January 8, 2019, was
  presented recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 19-04 amending Inglewood
  Municipal Code Chapter 12 (Planning and Zoning), Article 8 (“C-3” Heavy Commercial
  Zone Regulations) to include Zoning Code Amendment No. 2018-002 (ZCA-2018-002)
  to allow C-2A (Airport Commercial) zone permitted uses in the C-3 (Heavy Commercial)
  zone citywide.

  It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Franklin that further
  reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that Ordinance No. 19-04 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA TO
  AFFIRM AN EXEMPTION (EA-CE-2018-111) AND APPROVE
  ZONING CODE AMENDMENT 2018-002 (ZCA-2018-002) TO
  AMEND ARTICLE 8 OF CHAPTR 12 (PLANNING AND ZONING) OF
  THE INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE TO ALLOW C-2A (AIRPORT
  COMMERCIAL) ZONE PERMITTED USES IN C-3 (HEAVY
  COMMERCIAL) ZONE CITYWIDE

  which was introduced at the meeting held on December 11, 2018, be adopted. The
  motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 168  ORDINANCE NO. 19-05 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE CITY’S PERMIT
  PARKING DISTRICT ISSUANCE AND USE PROCEDURE DESCRIBED IN
  INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE CHAPTER 3 (MOTOR VEHICLES AND
  TRAFFIC), ARTICLE 2 (PARKING REGULATIONS), SECTION 3-78 (PERMIT
  ISSUANCE AND PROCEDURES). Staff report dated January 8, 2019, was presented
  recommending adoption of Ordinance No. 19-05 amending the City’s Permit Parking
  District Issuance and Use Procedure described in Inglewood Municipal Code Chapter 3
  (Motor Vehicles and Traffic), Article 2 (Parking Regulations), Section 3-78 (Permit
  Issuance and Procedures).

  It was moved by Council Member Franklin, and seconded by Council Member Morales
  that further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.
  4
 January 8, 2019

  Thereupon, It was moved by Mayor Butts, and seconded by Council Member Franklin
  that Ordinance No. 19-05 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA
  AMENDING INGLEWOOD MUNICIPAL CODE SECTION 3-78 TO ALLOW
  THE CITY TO USE VEHICLE LICENSE PLATE NUMBERS AS PARKING
  PERMITS FOR PARKING PERMITS DISTRICTS

  which was introduced at the meeting held December 11, 2018, be adopted. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Dotson, Padilla, Morales, Franklin and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

 219  ORAL REPORTS – CITY TREASURER. City Treasurer, Wanda Brown, wished
  everyone a Happy New Year. She commented that mortgage rates are falling and tax
  refunds will be issued during the Federal shut-down. She also asked the Mayor to close
  the meeting in memory of Mr. Henry Wise.
